title.zh: 卷一百十七 列傳第五十五: 徒單益都 粘哥荊山附:劉均 王賓附:王進等 國用安 時青
title.en: Volume 117 Biographies 55: Tudan Yidou, Zhan Gejingshan Relative: Liujun, Wang Bin Relative: Wang Jindeng, Guo Yongan, Shi Qing
title.raw: 卷一百十七 列傳第五十五: 徒單益都 粘哥荊山附:劉均 王賓附:王進等 國用安 時青 Volume 117 Biographies 55: Tudan Yidou, Zhan Gejingshan Relative: Liujun, Wang Bin Relative: Wang Jindeng, Guo Yongan, Shi Qing

sentences.zh: 徒單益都

translations.literal: Tudan Yidu
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Yidu

sentences.zh: 徒單益都，不詳其履歷，嘗累官為延安總管。

translations.literal: Tudan Yidu—his career is not recorded in detail; he had held successive offices and once served as zongguan of Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Yidu. His service record is not known in detail; he had risen through successive posts and once served as military commissioner of Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 正大九年正月，行省事於徐州。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year of Zhengda, he held office as branch secretariat commissioner at Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Zhengda 9 (1232), he was appointed to head the regional secretariat at Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時慶山奴撤東方之備入援，未至睢州，徐、邳義勝軍總領侯進、杜政、張興率本軍降大兵於永州。

translations.literal: At that time Qing Shannu withdrew the eastern defenses to bring relief; before reaching Suizhou, the commanders of the Yisheng Army of Xu and Pi—Hou Jin, Du Zheng, and Zhang Xing—led their units in surrendering to the great army at Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Qing Shannu had pulled troops from the east to march to the relief of the capital, but before he reached Suizhou, Hou Jin, Du Zheng, and Zhang Xing—the chiefs of the Yisheng Army in Xu and Pi—led their forces over to the Mongols at Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，大兵守徐張盆渡。

translations.literal: On the xinchou day, the great army held Zhangpen Ford in Xu.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinchou day, Mongol forces occupied Zhangpen Ford near Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 益都到官才三日，懼兵少不能守，即令移剌長壽率甲士千人迎大兵。

translations.literal: Yidu had been in office only three days; fearing his troops were too few to hold the city, he immediately ordered Yelü Changshou to lead a thousand armored soldiers to receive the great army.
translations.idiomatic: Yidu had been in his post only three days. Worried that he lacked the manpower to defend the city, he sent Yelü Changshou with a thousand armored troops to welcome the Mongol army.

sentences.zh: 長壽軍無紀律，大兵掩之，一軍皆覆，徐危甚。

translations.literal: Changshou's troops lacked discipline; the great army fell upon them in an ambush and the whole force was destroyed; the peril at Xu became extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Changshou's men were undisciplined. The Mongols struck in a surprise attack and annihilated the entire detachment, leaving Xuzhou in grave danger.

sentences.zh: 益都籍州人及運糧埽兵得萬人。

translations.literal: Yidu mustered ten thousand men from local residents and grain-transport scoop troops of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yidu drafted ten thousand men from among the townspeople and the grain-transport militia.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，大兵傅城，燒南關而去。

translations.literal: On the yisi day, the great army pressed close to the city walls, burned the southern gate district, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi day, the Mongols invested the city, torched the district outside the southern gate, and then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 侯進既降北，即以為京東行省，進遂請千人來襲。

translations.literal: After Hou Jin had defected to the north, he was made head of the eastern Hebei branch secretariat; Jin then requested a thousand men to come and raid the city.
translations.idiomatic: Once Hou Jin had gone over to the enemy, he was made commissioner of the eastern Hebei secretariat, and he asked for a thousand troops to launch a raid.

sentences.zh: 二月庚申，未明，大兵坎南城而上，守者皆散走，城中大呼曰：「大兵入南門矣！」

translations.literal: On the gengshen day of the second month, before dawn, the great army scaled the southern wall; the defenders all scattered and fled, and a great cry went up in the city: "The great army has entered the southern gate!"
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day of the second month, before dawn, Mongol troops climbed the southern wall. The defenders broke and ran, and voices throughout the city shouted, "The Mongols are through the southern gate!"

sentences.zh: 益都聞之不及甲，率州署夜直兵三百，由黃樓而南，力戰禦敵。

translations.literal: Yidu, hearing this, had no time to don armor; he led three hundred night-duty troops of the prefectural office south through Huanglou Tower and fought hard to repel the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Yidu had no time even to arm himself. He led three hundred men on night watch at the prefectural yamen south through Huanglou Tower and fought desperately to hold the enemy back.

sentences.zh: 亂定，遷賞有差。

translations.literal: When the disorder was settled, promotions and rewards were granted in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: After order was restored, men were promoted and rewarded according to their merit.

sentences.zh: 由是軍勢稍振，複奪張盆渡，取蕭縣，破白塔，戰于土山，救被俘老幼五千還徐。

translations.literal: From this the army's strength revived somewhat; they recovered Zhangpen Ford, took Xiao County, broke White Tower, fought at Tushan, and rescued five thousand old and young who had been captured, returning them to Xu.
translations.idiomatic: The army's morale rallied somewhat. They retook Zhangpen Ford, captured Xiao County, stormed White Tower, fought at Tushan, and brought five thousand captive old and young back to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 既而，侯進亡命駐靈璧，杜政、張興亦慮為北所害，窮窘自歸。

translations.literal: Before long Hou Jin, a fugitive, encamped at Lingbi; Du Zheng and Zhang Xing also feared harm from the northerners and, in desperate straits, returned of their own accord.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Hou Jin fled and camped at Lingbi. Du Zheng and Zhang Xing, fearing the northerners would kill them, came back in desperation.

sentences.zh: 益都撫而納之，興留徐，杜政還邳州。

translations.literal: Yidu comforted them and accepted them back; Xing remained at Xu, and Du Zheng returned to Pizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yidu received them kindly. Zhang Xing stayed at Xuzhou while Du Zheng went back to Pizhou.

sentences.zh: 益都資稟仁厚，持大體，二子兩侄為軍將，頗侵漁軍民。

translations.literal: Yidu was by nature benevolent and magnanimous and upheld the larger interest, but his two sons and two nephews served as army officers and greatly preyed upon soldiers and civilians.
translations.idiomatic: Yidu was a man of generous temperament who kept sight of the larger good, but his two sons and two nephews were army officers and preyed heavily on troops and civilians alike.

sentences.zh: 青州人王祐為埽兵總領。

translations.literal: Wang You of Qingzhou served as chief of the scoop troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wang You of Qingzhou was chief of the scoop militia.

sentences.zh: 將兵千七百人，益都常倚之，雖有過亦不責。

translations.literal: He commanded seventeen hundred troops; Yidu often relied on him and, even when he was at fault, did not hold him accountable.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded seventeen hundred troops. Yidu leaned on him heavily and never punished him even when he was clearly in the wrong.

sentences.zh: 以故祐亦橫恣，與河間張祚、下邑令李閏、義勝都統封仙、遙授永州刺史成進忠輩，乘軍政廢弛，城中空虛。

translations.literal: For this reason You also acted with arrogant license; together with Zhang Zuo of Hejian, Magistrate Li Run of Xiayi, Yisheng Army commander Feng Xian, and Cheng Jinzhong of Yongzhou by remote appointment, among others, they took advantage of the collapse of military discipline while the city stood empty.
translations.idiomatic: Emboldened by this protection, You grew brazen. He joined Zhang Zuo of Hejian, Magistrate Li Run of Xiayi, Yisheng commander Feng Xian, and Cheng Jinzhong—nominally commissioner of Yongzhou—and others in exploiting the breakdown of military order while the city was defenseless.

sentences.zh: 以六月丁巳夜燒草場作亂。

translations.literal: On the night of the dingsi day of the sixth month they burned the hay yard and rose in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the dingsi day in the sixth month they set fire to the hay yard and staged a mutiny.

sentences.zh: 時張興臥病，祐恐事不成，起興與同行。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Xing lay ill in bed; You feared the affair would fail and roused Xing to go along with them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xing was bedridden at the time. You feared the plot would fail and had him dragged from his sickbed to join them.

sentences.zh: 益都疑左右皆叛，挈妻子縋城而出，就從宜眾僧奴及東面總領劉安國軍。

translations.literal: Yidu suspected that everyone around him had turned traitor; he took his wife and children and let himself down from the wall by rope, then joined the armies of Congyi Zhongsengnu and eastern commander Liu Anguo.
translations.idiomatic: Believing his entire entourage had turned against him, Yidu lowered his wife and children over the wall by rope and fled to the camps of Congyi Zhongsengnu and the eastern commander Liu Anguo.

sentences.zh: 張興推祐為都元帥，複懼祐圖己，遂誅祐，並張祚殺之。

translations.literal: Zhang Xing pushed You forward as supreme commander, but then feared You would plot against him; he therefore executed You and killed Zhang Zuo as well.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xing made You supreme commander, then grew afraid You would turn on him. He had You killed—and Zhang Zuo with him.

sentences.zh: 因大掠城中。

translations.literal: They then plundered the city on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: They then looted the city wholesale.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，國用安以行山東路尚書省事率兵至徐，張興率甲士迎之。

translations.literal: On the renxu day, Guo Yong'an, holding office as Shandong-route minister of the branch secretariat, led troops to Xu; Zhang Xing led armored soldiers to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: On the renxu day Guo Yong'an arrived at Xuzhou at the head of troops as Shandong-route minister of the secretariat. Zhang Xing went out with armored men to receive him.

sentences.zh: 用安輕騎而入，執興與其党十餘人，斬之於市，遂以封仙為元帥，兼節度使，主徐州。

translations.literal: Yong'an entered with a light escort, seized Xing and more than ten of his partisans, and beheaded them in the market; he then made Feng Xian supreme commander and concurrently military commissioner, putting him in charge of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yong'an rode in with only a light escort, seized Zhang Xing and more than ten of his followers, and had them beheaded in the marketplace. He installed Feng Xian as supreme commander and military commissioner of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 益都窘無所歸，乃奔宿州，節度使紇石烈阿虎以益都為人所逐不納，乃與諸將駐于城南。

translations.literal: Yidu, in distress with nowhere to go, fled to Suzhou; the military commissioner Heshenlie Ahu, on the grounds that Yidu had been driven out by others, would not admit him, and so he camped with his generals south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: With nowhere left to turn, Yidu fled to Suzhou. Commissioner Heshenlie Ahu refused him entry—Yidu had been driven from his post, he said—and Yidu encamped with his officers south of the walls.

sentences.zh: 時宿之鎮防軍有逃還者，阿虎以為叛歸亦不納。

translations.literal: At the time some of Suzhou's garrison troops who had fled returned; Ahu regarded them as defectors coming back and would not admit them either.
translations.idiomatic: Some of Suzhou's garrison troops who had deserted now came back. Ahu treated them as turncoats and shut them out as well.

sentences.zh: 城中鎮防千戶高臘哥，結小吏郭仲安，謀就徐州將士內外相應以取宿，因歸楊妙真。

translations.literal: Within the city the garrison chiliarch Gao Lage joined with petty clerk Guo Zhong'an to plot with the Xuzhou officers for a coordinated inside-and-outside strike to seize Suzhou and thereby submit to Yang Miaozhen.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the city, garrison chiliarch Gao Lage and petty clerk Guo Zhong'an plotted with the Xuzhou garrison for a coordinated assault from within and without, intending to hand Suzhou over to Yang Miaozhen.

sentences.zh: 甲戌夜半，開門納徐州總領王德全及妻弟高元哥軍。

translations.literal: At midnight on the jiaxu day they opened the gates and admitted the armies of Xuzhou commander Wang Dequan and his brother-in-law Gao Yuange.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight on the jiaxu day they opened the gates and let in the forces of Xuzhou commander Wang Dequan and his brother-in-law Gao Yuange.

sentences.zh: 劉安國尋亦入城，縛阿虎父子殺之。

translations.literal: Liu Anguo soon entered the city as well, bound Ahu and his son, and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Anguo entered the city soon after, bound Ahu and his son, and put them to death.

sentences.zh: 州中請益都主帥府事，益都不從，曰：「吾國家舊人，為將帥亦久，以資性疏迂，不能周防，遂失重鎮。

translations.literal: The prefecture asked Yidu to take charge of headquarters affairs; Yidu refused, saying: "I am an old servant of our state and have long been a commander, but by nature I am blunt and slow-witted and could not guard on every side, and so I lost a vital stronghold.
translations.idiomatic: The city asked Yidu to take command of headquarters affairs. He refused. "I am an old servant of the dynasty and have been a commander for many years," he said, "but I am dull and careless by nature and failed to guard on every side, and so I lost a vital stronghold.

sentences.zh: 今大事已去，方逃罪不暇，豈有改易髻發、奪人城池以降外方乎！」

translations.literal: Now the great cause is lost and I am barely escaping blame—how could I change my hair and dress, seize another's city, and surrender to outsiders!"
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty's cause is already lost and I am barely escaping blame—how could I cut my hair, seize another man's city, and go over to outsiders!"

sentences.zh: 即日，率官吏而行，至穀熟東，遇大兵，不屈而死。

translations.literal: That same day he led his officials on the road; east of Gushu he encountered the great army and died without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he set out with his officials. East of Gushu he met Mongol troops and died rather than submit.

sentences.zh: 徐州既歸海州，邳帥兀林答某亦讓印于杜政，遂送款于用安。

translations.literal: Once Xuzhou had submitted to Haizhou, the Pi commander Ulindamo also surrendered his seal to Du Zheng and then sent terms of submission to Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xuzhou had gone over to Haizhou, the Pi commander Ulindamo handed his seal to Du Zheng and submitted to Guo Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 已而宿州王德全、劉安國亦送款海州。

translations.literal: Before long Wang Dequan and Liu Anguo of Suzhou also sent submission to Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wang Dequan and Liu Anguo of Suzhou submitted to Haizhou as well.

sentences.zh: 惟益都不改髻發，以至於死雲。

translations.literal: Only Yidu did not change his hair and dress, even unto death—or so it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yidu refused to cut his hair and went to his death—so the record says.

sentences.zh: 粘哥荊山

translations.literal: Niange Jingshan
translations.idiomatic: Niange Jingshan

sentences.zh: 粘哥荊山，不知其所始，正大中，累官亳州節度使。

translations.literal: Niange Jingshan—his origins are unknown; in the Zhengda era he held successive offices and became military commissioner of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Niange Jingshan. His origins are not recorded. During the Zhengda era he rose through successive posts to military commissioner of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 九年正月己丑，游騎自鄧至亳，鈔鹿邑，營于衛真西北五十里。

translations.literal: On the jichou day of the first month of the ninth year, roaming cavalry came from Deng to Bo, raided Luyi, and encamped fifty li northwest of Weizhen.
translations.idiomatic: On the jichou day of the first month of the ninth year, Mongol scouting horsemen came from Dengzhou to Bozhou, raided Luyi, and camped fifty li northwest of Weizhen.

sentences.zh: 鹿邑令高昂霄知太康已降，即夜趨亳，道出衛真，呼縣令楚珩約同行。

translations.literal: Luyi magistrate Gao Angxiao, learning that Taikang had already surrendered, hurried by night toward Bo; his route passed through Weizhen, and he called on Magistrate Chu Heng to travel together.
translations.idiomatic: When Luyi magistrate Gao Angxiao learned that Taikang had already fallen, he set out by night for Bozhou. His route took him through Weizhen, where he called on Magistrate Chu Heng to flee with him.

sentences.zh: 珩知勢不支，即明諭縣人以避遷之意，遂同走亳。

translations.literal: Heng knew the situation could not be sustained; he openly informed the county people of his intent to flee the relocation, and then fled with him to Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Heng saw the situation was hopeless. He openly told the county people he meant to evacuate, then fled with Gao to Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 丁未，二邑皆降。

translations.literal: On the dingwei day both counties surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingwei day both counties submitted.

sentences.zh: 是日，軍至亳州城下。

translations.literal: That same day the army reached the walls of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the army reached the walls of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 州止有單州兵四百人，號「鎮安軍」，提控楊春、邢某、都統戴興屯已六年。

translations.literal: The prefecture had only four hundred troops from Danzhou, called the "Pacifying-the-Realm Army"; commanders Yang Chun, Xing Mou, and commander-in-chief Dai Xing had been garrisoned there for six years.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture had only four hundred troops from Danzhou, known as the "Pacifying-the-Realm Army." Commanders Yang Chun and Xing Mou and commander-in-chief Dai Xing had been stationed there for six years.

sentences.zh: 荊山悉籍城中丁壯為軍，修守具，而大兵亦不暇攻。

translations.literal: Jingshan registered all able-bodied men in the city as soldiers and repaired defensive equipment, while the great army also had no leisure to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshan drafted every able-bodied man in the city into the army and repaired the defenses. The Mongols, for their part, had no time to press the assault.

sentences.zh: 四月，擁降民而北，城門閉，不之知也。

translations.literal: In the fourth month they drove surrendered civilians northward; the city gates were closed and no one knew of it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the Mongols drove surrendered civilians northward. The gates were shut and the city knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 五月，縱遷民收麥，老幼得出，丁壯悉留之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month they allowed relocated civilians to harvest wheat; the old and young could go out, but all able-bodied men were kept.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month they let relocated civilians out to harvest wheat. The old and young were allowed to leave; every able-bodied man was held back.

sentences.zh: 民往往不肯留而遁，數日，城為之空。

translations.literal: The people often refused to stay and fled; within days the city was emptied on their account.
translations.idiomatic: Many refused to stay and slipped away. Within days the city was deserted.

sentences.zh: 荊山遣將領各詣所屬招之，並將領亦不返。

translations.literal: Jingshan sent officers each to his district to summon them back, but the officers themselves also did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshan sent officers to their home districts to round people up, but the officers never came back either.

sentences.zh: 「鎮安」者皆紅祆餘黨，力盡來歸，變詐反復，朝廷終以盜賊待之。

translations.literal: The men of "Pacifying-the-Realm" were all remnants of the Red Scarves; when their strength was spent they came over, but they were changeable, deceitful, and treacherous, and the court always treated them as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The "Pacifying-the-Realm" troops were remnants of the Red Scarves. When their strength was spent they submitted, but they were treacherous and fickle, and the court always treated them as bandits.

sentences.zh: 荊山以遷民為軍，蓋防之也。

translations.literal: Jingshan made the relocated civilians into an army—this was essentially to guard against them.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshan drafted the relocated civilians into an army chiefly to keep them under control.

sentences.zh: 及召外兵不至，乃請於歸德，得甲騎百餘，兩總領統之。

translations.literal: When summoned outside troops did not arrive, he requested aid from Guide and obtained a little more than a hundred armored cavalry, with two commanders leading them.
translations.idiomatic: When outside reinforcements failed to arrive, he asked Guide for help and received a little over a hundred armored horsemen under two commanders.

sentences.zh: 既至，「鎮安」疑其謀己，乃乘將士新到不設備，至夜，掩殺殆盡。

translations.literal: Once they arrived, the Pacifying-the-Realm men suspected a plot against themselves; taking advantage of the troops' recent arrival and lack of preparedness, they fell upon them at night and killed nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived, the "Pacifying-the-Realm" troops suspected a plot against them. The newcomers were unprepared; at night the garrison fell on them and killed nearly every man.

sentences.zh: 荊山出走衛真，楚珩與之馬而去，州中豪貴悉被剽略。

translations.literal: Jingshan fled toward Weizhen; Chu Heng gave him a horse and he departed, while the wealthy and eminent of the prefecture were all plundered.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshan fled toward Weizhen. Chu Heng gave him a horse and he escaped. The wealthy families of the prefecture were looted clean.

sentences.zh: 劉堅者，初為大兵守城父，亳州複，擒之，囚之於獄。

translations.literal: There was one Liu Jian, who had first served the great army in defending Chengfù; when Bozhou was recovered he was captured and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian had first served the Mongols as defender of Chengfù. When Bozhou was retaken he was captured and thrown in prison.

sentences.zh: 楊春謀欲北降，乃出之，使為宣差。

translations.literal: Yang Chun plotted to defect northward; he released him and made him an imperial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chun planned to defect to the north. He released Liu Jian and made him an imperial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，大兵石總管入州，改州為順天府，春為總管，戴興為同知，劉順治中，留党項軍千人戍之。

translations.literal: On the yisi day the great army's Commissioner Shi entered the prefecture; the prefecture was renamed Shuntian Prefecture; Chun became commissioner, Dai Xing became vice commissioner, Liu Shun became administrative supervisor, and a thousand Tangut troops were left to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi day Mongol Commissioner Shi entered the city. The prefecture was renamed Shuntian. Yang Chun became commissioner, Dai Xing vice commissioner, and Liu Shun administrative supervisor. A thousand Tangut troops were left as garrison.

sentences.zh: 屬縣皆下，惟城父令李用宜不降，其妻子在亳，春以為質，竟不屈而死。

translations.literal: All subordinate counties submitted; only Chengfù magistrate Li Yongyi would not surrender. His wife and children were in Bo; Chun held them as hostages, but in the end he refused to yield and died.
translations.idiomatic: Every subordinate county submitted. Only Chengfù magistrate Li Yongyi held out. Yang Chun took his wife and children at Bozhou as hostages, but Li refused to yield and died.

sentences.zh: 春既據州，與劉堅坐樓上，召副提控邢某。

translations.literal: Once Chun held the prefecture, he and Liu Jian sat in a tower and summoned deputy commander Xing Mou.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yang Chun held the city, he and Liu Jian sat in a tower and sent for deputy commander Xing Mou.

sentences.zh: 邢剛直循理，將士嚴憚之，時臥病，聞春亂，流涕不自禁。

translations.literal: Xing was upright and followed reason; officers and soldiers stood in awe of him. He lay ill at the time; hearing of Chun's mutiny, he wept uncontrollably.
translations.idiomatic: Xing was a man of stern integrity whom officers and men alike feared. He was bedridden when he heard of Yang Chun's revolt and wept uncontrollably.

sentences.zh: 春遣人舁致之，邢指春大罵，春慚恧無言。

translations.literal: Chun sent men to carry him there; Xing pointed at Chun and reviled him loudly; Chun was ashamed and speechless.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chun had him carried in. Xing pointed at him and cursed him to his face. Yang Chun stood silent with shame.

sentences.zh: 春欲殺荊山家，邢力勸止之，且令給道路費送之出城，邢尋病卒。

translations.literal: Chun wished to kill Jingshan's family; Xing strongly urged him to stop and also ordered travel expenses given to send them out of the city; Xing soon died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chun wanted to slaughter Jingshan's family. Xing talked him out of it and had travel money provided to send them out of the city. Xing soon died of his illness.

sentences.zh: 二年夏四月，北省忒木泬攻歸德，春以戴興提精卒以往，獨與疲弱者守城。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer of the second year, the northern province's Temüge attacked Guide; Chun sent Dai Xing with picked troops to go, and remained alone with the weak to guard the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer in the second year, Temüge of the northern command attacked Guide. Yang Chun sent Dai Xing with elite troops while he stayed behind with only the weak to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 州人王賓遂反正，春渡河北遁。

translations.literal: The Bozhou man Wang Bin then restored allegiance to the right side; Chun crossed the river north and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bin of Bozhou then restored the city to Jin allegiance. Yang Chun fled north across the river.

sentences.zh: 既而崔七斤為亂，殺王賓。

translations.literal: Before long Cui Qijin stirred up disorder and killed Wang Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Cui Qijin mutinied and killed Wang Bin.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不得已，以七斤為節度使，就其兵仗入蔡。

translations.literal: The court, having no choice, made Qijin military commissioner and took his troops and weapons into Cai.
translations.idiomatic: The court had no choice but to make Qijin military commissioner and march his troops and arms into Cai.

sentences.zh: 八月，劉順攻亳州，破之，七斤為城父令所殺。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Liu Shun attacked Bozhou, broke it, and Qijin was killed by the Chengfù magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Liu Shun attacked Bozhou, took it, and Qijin was killed by the magistrate of Chengfù.

sentences.zh: 未幾，單州軍以州人殺其家屬，召大兵來攻，蚧能拔，殺屬縣民而去。

translations.literal: Before long the Danzhou army, because locals had killed their families, summoned the great army to attack; Nie Nengba pulled out and killed people of the subordinate counties as he departed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Danzhou garrison, whose families had been killed by locals, called in the Mongols to attack. Nie Nengba withdrew after slaughtering people in the subordinate counties.

sentences.zh: 既渡河，知亳人不疑，複來攻，州竟為春所破。

translations.literal: After crossing the river, knowing the people of Bo were off guard, he attacked again; in the end the prefecture was broken by Chun.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing the river he found the people of Bozhou unprepared and attacked again. In the end Yang Chun retook the city.

sentences.zh: 是年六月，宋人來攻，春出降，劉堅北走。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of that year the Song came to attack; Chun surrendered and Liu Jian fled north.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of that year the Song attacked. Yang Chun surrendered and Liu Jian fled north.

sentences.zh: 附:劉均

translations.literal: Appended: Liu Jun
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Liu Jun

sentences.zh: 劉均者，林慮人，時為亳州觀察判官。

translations.literal: Liu Jun was a man of Linlu and at the time served as Bozhou surveillance administrative judge.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun was a native of Linlu and at the time served as administrative judge of Bozhou surveillance.

sentences.zh: 春既逐荊山，納款大兵，脅均同降。

translations.literal: After Chun had driven out Jingshan and submitted to the great army, he coerced Jun to surrender along with him.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Chun had driven out Jingshan and submitted to the Mongols, he pressured Liu Jun to surrender as well.

sentences.zh: 均佯應之，歸其家取朝服服之， 顧謂妻子曰：「我起身刀筆，仰荷上知，始列朝著，又佐大籓，死亦足矣。

translations.literal: Jun pretended to agree; he returned home, put on court robes, and turning to his wife and children said: "I rose from the clerk's brush, received the sovereign's grace, first took my place at court, and then served a great frontier post—death is enough.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun pretended to agree. He went home, dressed in his court robes, and said to his wife and children: "I began as a clerk and rose only by the emperor's grace. I have stood at court and served a great frontier post. Death is enough for me.

sentences.zh: 今頭顱已如此，假使有十年壽，何以見先帝於地下乎。」

translations.literal: Now my head is already in this condition; even if I had ten years of life, how could I face the former emperor in the underworld?"
translations.idiomatic: My head is already forfeit. Even if I lived ten more years, how could I face the late emperor in the grave?"

sentences.zh: 即仰藥而死。

translations.literal: He then took poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: He drank poison and died.

sentences.zh: 王賓，字德卿，亳州人。

translations.literal: Wang Bin, style Deqing, was a man of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bin, courtesy name Deqing, was a native of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Zhenyou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the civil service examination in Zhenyou 2 (1214).

sentences.zh: 外若曠達，而深有謀畫。

translations.literal: Outwardly he seemed free and easy, but inwardly he was deeply resourceful in planning.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly he seemed easygoing, but he was a man of deep strategic ability.

sentences.zh: 初調蘭陵主簿，辟虹縣令，尋入為尚書省令史，坐事罷歸鄉里。

translations.literal: He was first appointed chief clerk of Lanling, then summoned as magistrate of Hong County; soon after he entered service as a clerk of the Ministry of Revenue and, implicated in an affair, was dismissed and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: He was first posted as chief clerk of Lanling, then appointed magistrate of Hong County. He soon entered the Ministry of Revenue as a clerk, but was dismissed after an offense and returned home.

sentences.zh: 天興元年正月，亳州軍變，節度使粘哥荊山出走，楊春以州出降。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Tianxing the Bozhou army mutinied; military commissioner Niange Jingshan fled, and Yang Chun surrendered the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Tianxing 1 (1232), the Bozhou garrison mutinied. Commissioner Niange Jingshan fled and Yang Chun surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 既而，自以羸兵守之。

translations.literal: Before long he himself held it with weakened troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chun soon found himself holding the city with only a weakened garrison.

sentences.zh: 賓與前譙縣尉王進、魏節亨、呂鈞約城中軍民複其州，楊春遂遁，遣節亨詣歸德以聞。

translations.literal: Bin joined with former Qiao County lieutenant Wang Jin, Wei Jieheng, and Lü Jun in plotting with the city's soldiers and civilians to restore the prefecture; Yang Chun then fled, and they sent Jieheng to Guide to report it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bin joined former Qiao County lieutenant Wang Jin, Wei Jieheng, and Lü Jun in rallying the city's troops and people to restore Jin rule. Yang Chun fled. They sent Jieheng to Guide to report the success.

sentences.zh: 哀宗嘉之，授進節度使，賓同知節度使，節亨節度副使，鈞觀察判官。

translations.literal: Emperor Aizong praised this and appointed Jin military commissioner, Bin vice military commissioner, Jieheng deputy military commissioner, and Jun surveillance administrative judge.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Aizong commended them and appointed Wang Jin military commissioner, Wang Bin vice commissioner, Wei Jieheng deputy commissioner, and Lü Jun surveillance judge.

sentences.zh: 楊春複以兵來攻，月餘不能拔，即渡河而北。

translations.literal: Yang Chun again came to attack with troops; for more than a month he could not take it, and then crossed the river northward.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chun attacked again with an army but could not take the city for more than a month and withdrew north across the river.

sentences.zh: 六月，哀宗遷蔡，賓奉迎於州北之高安。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Emperor Aizong moved to Cai; Bin went to welcome him at Gao'an north of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Emperor Aizong moved the court to Cai. Wang Bin went north of the city to Gao'an to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 上與語，大悅，恨用之晚，擢為行部尚書、世襲謀克。

translations.literal: The emperor spoke with him and was greatly pleased, regretting that he had been employed too late; he promoted him to acting minister of the department and hereditary mouke.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor spoke with him and was delighted, regretting only that he had not been used sooner. He promoted him to acting minister of the department and hereditary mouke.

sentences.zh: 上初至亳，賓等適征民丁負鐵甲入蔡，及會計忠孝軍家屬口糧，故留參知政事張天綱董之，就遷有功將士。

translations.literal: When the emperor first reached Bo, Bin and the others happened to be conscripting civilian laborers to carry iron armor into Cai and tallying grain rations for the families of the Loyal-and-Filial Army; therefore they left Participating Councilor Zhang Tiangang to supervise this and promote meritorious officers and soldiers on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first reached Bozhou, Wang Bin and his colleagues were conscripting civilians to haul iron armor to Cai and tallying grain rations for the families of the Loyal-and-Filial Army. They left Participating Councilor Zhang Tiangang behind to oversee this work and promote deserving officers.

sentences.zh: 時亳之糧儲不廣，賓等常吝惜，軍士以此歸怨。

translations.literal: At the time Bozhou's grain stores were not ample; Bin and the others were often stingy, and for this the soldiers bore resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhou's grain stores were meager at the time, and Wang Bin and his colleagues were stingy with rations. The troops resented them for it.

sentences.zh: 及運甲之役，複不欲行。

translations.literal: When the task of transporting armor came, they again did not wish to go.
translations.idiomatic: When the armor transport duty came up, they refused to go again.

sentences.zh: 會天綱與賓等於一樓上銓次立功等第，鎮防軍崔複哥、王六十之徒擐甲嘩噪登樓，天綱問曰：「即欲見殺，容我望闕拜辭。」

translations.literal: When Tiangang and Bin were on a tower ranking grades of merit for those who had earned distinction, garrison troops such as Cui Fuge and Wang Liushi, armored and clamoring, stormed up the tower; Tiangang asked: "If you mean to kill me now, allow me to bow toward the palace and take leave."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tiangang and Wang Bin were on a tower ranking men by merit when garrison troops led by Cui Fuge and Wang Liushi, armed and shouting, stormed upstairs. Zhang Tiangang said, "If you mean to kill me, let me bow toward the palace first."

sentences.zh: 賊曰：「無預相公。」

translations.literal: The rebels said: "It has nothing to do with the lord counselor."
translations.idiomatic: The mutineers said, "This has nothing to do with you, Chancellor."

sentences.zh: 即拽賓及呂鈞往市中。

translations.literal: They then dragged Bin and Lü Jun toward the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: They dragged Wang Bin and Lü Jun down into the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 鈞且行且跪，涕淚俱下。

translations.literal: Jun went along kneeling as he walked, tears streaming down.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Jun went along on his knees, weeping as he went.

sentences.zh: 賓岸然不懼，大叫曰：「不過殺我。

translations.literal: Bin stood firm without fear and shouted: "Nothing more than killing me.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bin stood erect and unafraid. He shouted, "You can only kill me.

sentences.zh: 但殺，但殺！」

translations.literal: Just kill, just kill!"
translations.idiomatic: Go on—kill me, kill me!"

sentences.zh: 乃並害之。

translations.literal: They then killed them all together.
translations.idiomatic: They killed them both.

sentences.zh: 節度副使魏節亨、節度判官孫良、觀察副使孫九住皆被害。

translations.literal: Deputy military commissioner Wei Jieheng, military commissioner judge Sun Liang, and surveillance deputy Sun Jiuzhu were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commissioner Wei Jieheng, commissioner judge Sun Liang, and surveillance deputy Sun Jiuzhu were killed as well.

sentences.zh: 又數日，殺節度使王進。

translations.literal: A few days later they killed military commissioner Wang Jin.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later they killed Military Commissioner Wang Jin.

sentences.zh: 進嘗應荊山之募，由間道入汴京納奏，賞以物不受，又散家所有濟貧民，以死自勵。

translations.literal: Jin had once answered Jingshan's call for recruits, entered Bianjing by a secret route to deliver a memorial, refused rewards of goods, and also distributed all his household possessions to aid the poor, taking death as his inspiration.
translations.idiomatic: Jin had once answered Jingshan's call for recruits and slipped into Kaifeng by a back road to deliver a memorial. He refused rewards of goods and gave away his entire household fortune to help the poor, steeling himself for death.

sentences.zh: 至汴，以勞遷本州節度判官。

translations.literal: When he reached Bian he was transferred for his labors to military commissioner judge of his home prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Kaifeng he was promoted to military commissioner judge of his home prefecture in recognition of his service.

sentences.zh: 賜以白金，亦不受，一時甚稱之。

translations.literal: He was granted white silver but again would not accept it; for a time he was greatly praised.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered silver but refused that as well. For a time he was widely praised.

sentences.zh: 附:王進 等

translations.literal: Appended: Wang Jin and others
translations.idiomatic: Appended biographies: Wang Jin and others

sentences.zh: 有李喜住者，本宿州眾僧奴下宣差。

translations.literal: There was one Li Xizhu, originally an imperial commissioner under Zhongsengnu of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: There was a man named Li Xizhu, originally an imperial commissioner under Zhongsengnu of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 天興二年四月，進糧入歸德，將還，聞亳州王進反正，制旨以喜住為振武都尉，將兵三千應援。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Tianxing he brought grain into Guide and was about to return when he heard that Wang Jin of Bozhou had restored allegiance; an imperial order made Xizhu Zhenwu commander and sent him with three thousand troops to reinforce.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Tianxing 2 he delivered grain to Guide and was about to return when he heard that Wang Jin of Bozhou had restored the city to Jin rule. An imperial order made Xizhu commander of the Zhenwu Guard and sent him with three thousand men to reinforce the city.

sentences.zh: 是時，太赤圍亳步騎十萬，喜住以眾寡不敵，獨與三人間道入城，王進方議遷左軍林，喜住不可，進即以兵付喜住。

translations.literal: At that time Taichi besieged Bo with a hundred thousand infantry and cavalry; Xizhu, seeing his force too few to match them, entered the city alone with three men by a secret route; Wang Jin was just discussing moving to Zuojunlin, which Xizhu forbade, and Jin then handed his troops over to Xizhu.
translations.idiomatic: Taichi was then besieging Bozhou with a hundred thousand foot and horse. Outnumbered, Xizhu entered the city by a secret route with only three companions. Wang Jin was discussing a move to Zuojunlin, which Xizhu opposed, and Jin handed his troops over to him.

sentences.zh: 大兵攻八日不能下。

translations.literal: The great army attacked for eight days but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: The Mongols assaulted the city for eight days without success.

sentences.zh: 五月壬子，兵退。

translations.literal: On the renzi day of the fifth month the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: On the renzi day of the fifth month the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 己未，官奴與阿裏合提忠孝軍百人至亳，與諸將議遷可否。

translations.literal: On the jiwei day Guannu and Aliheti arrived at Bo with a hundred men of the Loyal-and-Filial Army and discussed with the generals whether relocation was advisable.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiwei day Guannu and Aliheti arrived at Bozhou with a hundred Loyal-and-Filial troops to discuss with the generals whether the court should move.

sentences.zh: 以為不可，當留輜重于蔡，選軍扈從入聖朵就武仙軍，遂入關中。

translations.literal: They held it inadvisable; baggage should be left at Cai, picked troops should escort the emperor into Shengdou to join Wu Xian's army, and then they should enter Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: They argued against it. Baggage should be left at Cai, picked troops should escort the emperor to Shengdou to join Wu Xian's army, and then they should enter the Guanzhong region.

sentences.zh: 關中地利可恃，又有郭蝦蟆等軍在西可恃。

translations.literal: Guanzhong's terrain could be relied upon, and moreover Guo Xiamo's army and others in the west could be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: The terrain of Guanzhong was defensible, and Guo Xiamo's army and other forces in the west could be counted on.

sentences.zh: 五月甲子，召官奴還歸德，不赴，再召，留其軍半於亳乃赴。

translations.literal: On the jiazi day of the fifth month Guannu was summoned back to Guide but did not go; summoned again, he left half his army at Bo and then went.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day of the fifth month Guannu was summoned back to Guide but refused to go. Summoned a second time, he left half his army at Bozhou and then set out.

sentences.zh: 六月壬辰，車駕舟行至亳，王進奏：「臣本軍伍，不知治體，如李喜住扈從入蔡，則毫不守矣。

translations.literal: On the renchen day of the sixth month the imperial carriage arrived at Bo by boat; Wang Jin memorialized: "Your servant is of the army ranks and does not understand governance; if Li Xizhu escorts Your Majesty into Cai, this place will be utterly undefended.
translations.idiomatic: On the renchen day of the sixth month the imperial barge reached Bozhou. Wang Jin memorialized: "I am a soldier and know nothing of civil administration. If Li Xizhu escorts Your Majesty to Cai, this city will be left utterly undefended.

sentences.zh: 乞留治此州。」

translations.literal: I beg to be left to govern this prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: I beg to be left behind to govern this prefecture."

sentences.zh: 詔以喜住為集慶軍節度使，便宜從事，進領帥職。

translations.literal: An edict made Xizhu military commissioner of the Jiqing Army with discretionary authority, and Jin took command of headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Xizhu military commissioner of the Jiqing Army with discretionary authority, while Jin took command of headquarters.

sentences.zh: 七月，進死。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Jin died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Wang Jin was killed.

sentences.zh: 喜住先往城父督糧餫，聞亂遂不敢入亳，後投宋。

translations.literal: Xizhu had gone first to Chengfù to supervise grain transport; hearing of the disorder he dared not enter Bo and later defected to the Song.
translations.idiomatic: Xizhu had gone ahead to Chengfù to supervise grain shipments. Hearing of the mutiny he dared not enter Bozhou and later went over to the Song.

sentences.zh: 論曰：金季之亂，軍士欲代其偏裨，偏裨欲代其主將，即群起而僨之。

translations.literal: The commentary says: In the disorders of the late Jin, soldiers wished to replace their company officers, company officers wished to replace their commanders, and they would rise in groups and overthrow them.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: In the disorders of the late Jin, soldiers sought to replace their company officers, company officers sought to replace their commanders, and mobs would rise up to overthrow them.

sentences.zh: 無複忌憚。

translations.literal: There was no longer any restraint or fear.
translations.idiomatic: No restraint or fear remained.

sentences.zh: 益都、荊山皆忠亮之士，賓、進才略尤足取焉，而並不免於難，惜哉！

translations.literal: Yidu and Jingshan were both loyal and upright men; Bin and Jin were especially worthy for their talent and strategy, yet none escaped disaster—how regrettable!
translations.idiomatic: Yidu and Jingshan were men of loyalty and integrity; Wang Bin and Wang Jin were especially admirable for their talent and strategy—yet none escaped disaster. What a pity!

sentences.zh: 國用安

translations.literal: Guo Yong'an
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yong'an

sentences.zh: 國用安，先名安用，本名咬兒，淄州人。

translations.literal: Guo Yong'an, formerly named Anyong, original name Yao'er, was a man of Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yong'an, formerly called Anyong and originally named Yao'er, was a native of Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 紅祆賊楊安兒、李全餘黨也。

translations.literal: He was a remnant follower of the Red Scarves bandits Yang An'er and Li Quan.
translations.idiomatic: He was a remnant of the Red Scarves rebels Yang An'er and Li Quan.

sentences.zh: 嘗歸順大元，為都元帥、行山東路尚書省事。

translations.literal: He had once submitted to the Great Yuan and served as supreme commander and Shandong-route minister of the branch secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He had once submitted to the Mongols and served as supreme commander and Shandong-route minister of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 天興元年六月，徐州埽兵總領王祐、義勝軍都統封仙、總領張興等夜燒草場作亂，逐元帥徒單益都。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Tianxing, Xuzhou scoop-troop chief Wang You, Yisheng Army commander Feng Xian, commander Zhang Xing, and others burned the hay yard by night and rose in revolt, driving out supreme commander Tudan Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Tianxing 1, Xuzhou militia chief Wang You, Yisheng commander Feng Xian, commander Zhang Xing, and others burned the hay yard by night and mutinied, driving out Supreme Commander Tudan Yidu.

sentences.zh: 安用率兵入徐，執張興與其党十餘人斬之，以封仙為元帥兼節度使，主徐州。

translations.literal: Anyong led troops into Xu, seized Zhang Xing and more than ten of his partisans and beheaded them, made Feng Xian supreme commander and concurrently military commissioner, and put him in charge of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Anyong led troops into Xuzhou, seized Zhang Xing and more than ten of his followers and beheaded them, and installed Feng Xian as supreme commander and military commissioner of the city.

sentences.zh: 宿州鎮防軍千戶高臘哥與東面總帥劉安國構徐州總帥王德全，殺宿帥紇石烈阿虎，以其州歸海州。

translations.literal: Suzhou garrison chiliarch Gao Lage and eastern commander Liu Anguo plotted with Xuzhou commander Wang Dequan, killed Suzhou commander Heshenlie Ahu, and submitted the prefecture to Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Suzhou garrison chiliarch Gao Lage and eastern commander Liu Anguo conspired with Xuzhou commander Wang Dequan, killed Suzhou commissioner Heshenlie Ahu, and handed the prefecture over to Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 邳州從宜兀林答某亦讓州于杜政，送款海州。

translations.literal: Pizhou congyi Ulindamo also yielded the prefecture to Du Zheng and sent submission to Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pizhou congyi Ulindamo also handed his prefecture to Du Zheng and submitted to Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 既而皆歸安用。

translations.literal: Before long all submitted to Anyong.
translations.idiomatic: Before long all came under Anyong's control.

sentences.zh: 北大將阿術魯聞安用據徐、宿、邳，大怒曰：「此三州我當攻取，安用何人，輒受降。」

translations.literal: The northern general Ashulu, hearing that Anyong held Xu, Su, and Pi, said in great anger: "These three prefectures I ought to attack and take—who is Anyong to accept their surrender on his own?"
translations.idiomatic: The Mongol general Ashulu, learning that Anyong held Xu, Su, and Pi, flew into a rage. "Those three prefectures are mine to take," he said. "Who is Anyong to accept their surrender on his own?"

sentences.zh: 遣信安、張進等率兵入徐，欲圖安用，奪其軍。

translations.literal: He sent Xin'an, Zhang Jin, and others to lead troops into Xu, intending to plot against Anyong and seize his army.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Xin'an, Zhang Jin, and others with troops into Xuzhou, intending to destroy Anyong and seize his army.

sentences.zh: 安用懼，謀于德全，劫殺張進及海州元帥田福等數百人，與楊妙真絕，乃還邳州。

translations.literal: Anyong was afraid; he plotted with Dequan, ambushed and killed Zhang Jin and Haizhou commander Tian Fu and several hundred others, broke with Yang Miaozhen, and then returned to Pizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Anyong was terrified. He plotted with Dequan, ambushed and killed Zhang Jin and Haizhou commander Tian Fu along with several hundred others, broke with Yang Miaozhen, and withdrew to Pizhou.

sentences.zh: 會山東諸將及徐、宿、邳主帥，刑馬結盟，誓歸金朝。

translations.literal: He gathered the generals of Shandong and the commanders of Xu, Su, and Pi, slaughtered a horse to seal an alliance, and swore to return to the Jin court.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered the Shandong generals and the commanders of Xu, Su, and Pi, slaughtered a horse to seal an alliance, and swore to return to the Jin dynasty.

sentences.zh: 既盟，諸將皆散去，安用無所歸，遂同德全、安國托從宜眾僧奴自通於朝廷。

translations.literal: After the alliance the generals all dispersed; Anyong had nowhere to go, and so together with Dequan and Anguo he had congyi Zhongsengnu communicate with the court on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: After the oath the generals dispersed. With nowhere to turn, Anyong had congyi Zhongsengnu open communications with the court on his behalf, together with Dequan and Anguo.

sentences.zh: 眾僧奴遣人上奏：「安用以數州反正，功甚大。

translations.literal: Zhongsengnu sent a man to memorialize: "Anyong has restored several prefectures to allegiance; his merit is very great.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsengnu sent a memorial: "Anyong has restored several prefectures to Jin allegiance. His merit is very great.

sentences.zh: 且其兵力強盛，材略可稱。

translations.literal: Moreover his military strength is formidable and his talent and strategy are commendable.
translations.idiomatic: His forces are strong and his talent and strategy are considerable.

sentences.zh: 國家果欲倚用，非極品重權不足以堅其許國之心。」

translations.literal: If the state truly wishes to rely on him, nothing short of the highest rank and weighty authority will suffice to firm his heart in service to the state."
translations.idiomatic: If the court truly means to rely on him, nothing short of the highest rank and greatest authority will bind his loyalty."

sentences.zh: 未報。

translations.literal: No reply came.
translations.idiomatic: No reply came.

sentences.zh: 安用率兵萬人攻海州，未至，眾稍散去。

translations.literal: Anyong led ten thousand troops to attack Haizhou; before he arrived his force had already begun to scatter somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Anyong led ten thousand men against Haizhou, but before he arrived his troops had already begun to drift away.

sentences.zh: 安國因勸安用當赤心歸國，安用亦自知反復失計，事已無可奈何，於是複金朝衣冠。

translations.literal: Anguo therefore urged Anyong to return to the state with a loyal heart; Anyong also knew himself that his vacillation had been a mistake and that matters were now beyond remedy, and so he resumed Jin court dress.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo urged Anyong to return to the Jin with a loyal heart. Anyong knew his vacillation had been a fatal mistake and that there was no turning back, and he resumed Jin court dress.

sentences.zh: 妙真怒其叛己，又懼為所圖，悉屠安用家走益都。

translations.literal: Miaozhen was enraged that he had betrayed her and also feared being plotted against; she slaughtered all of Anyong's family and fled to Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Miaozhen was furious at his betrayal and feared he would move against her. She slaughtered his entire family and fled to Yidu.

sentences.zh: 安用遂選兵分將，期必得妙真，自此淮海之上無寧歲矣。

translations.literal: Anyong then picked troops and assigned generals, resolved to capture Miaozhen at all costs; from this time onward there was no peaceful year on the Huai-Hai coast.
translations.idiomatic: Anyong then picked troops and assigned generals, determined to capture Miaozhen at any cost. From that time on the Huai-Hai coast knew no peace.

sentences.zh: 未幾，朝廷遣近侍局直長因世英、都事高天祐持手詔至邳，以安用為開府儀同三司、平章政事、兼都元帥、京東山東等路行尚書省事，特封兗王，賜號「英烈戡難保節忠臣」，錫姓完顏，附屬籍，改名用安，賜金鍍銀印、駝紐金印、金虎符、世襲千戶宣命、敕樣、牌樣、禦畫體宣、空頭河朔山東赦文，便宜從事，且以彭王妃誥委用安招妙真。

translations.literal: Before long the court sent Palace Attendant Bureau chief Yin Shiying and bureau director Gao Tianyou bearing an autograph edict to Pi; Anyong was made Grand Preceptor with the same ceremonial privileges as the Three Excellencies, Grand Councilor, and concurrently supreme commander and eastern Hebei and Shandong-route minister of the branch secretariat; he was specially enfeoffed as Prince of Yan, granted the title "Heroic and Loyal, Quelling Hardship and Preserving Integrity, Faithful Minister," given the surname Wanyan and attached to the imperial clan register, renamed Yong'an, and granted a gold-plated silver seal, a camel-knob gold seal, a gold tiger tally, a hereditary thousand-household commission, edict forms, plaque forms, an imperial brush announcement, and blank amnesty documents for Hebei and Shandong, with discretionary authority; moreover the patent of Princess Peng was entrusted to Yong'an to recruit Miaozhen.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the court sent Palace Attendant Bureau chief Yin Shiying and director Gao Tianyou with an autograph edict to Pizhou. Anyong was made Grand Preceptor with ceremonial privileges equal to the Three Excellencies, Grand Councilor, and concurrently supreme commander and minister of the eastern Hebei and Shandong secretariat. He was enfeoffed as Prince of Yan and granted the title "Heroic and Loyal, Quelling Hardship and Preserving Integrity, Faithful Minister." He was given the surname Wanyan, enrolled in the imperial clan register, and renamed Yong'an. He received a gold-plated silver seal, a camel-knob gold seal, a gold tiger tally, a hereditary thousand-household commission, edict and plaque forms, an imperial brush announcement, and blank amnesty documents for Hebei and Shandong, with full discretionary authority. The patent of Princess Peng was entrusted to him to win over Yang Miaozhen.

sentences.zh: 用安始聞使者至，猶豫未決，以總領楊懋迎使者入，監於州廨，問所以來。

translations.literal: When Yong'an first heard the envoys had arrived he hesitated and had not decided; he had commander Yang Mao welcome the envoys in, detained them at the prefectural offices, and asked the purpose of their coming.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong'an first heard the envoys had arrived he hesitated. He had Commander Yang Mao welcome them in, detained them at the prefectural offices, and asked why they had come.

sentences.zh: 世英對以封建事，意頗順。

translations.literal: Shiying answered regarding the enfeoffment; his manner was rather compliant.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying spoke of the enfeoffment in accommodating terms.

sentences.zh: 諸帥王、杜輩皆不欲宣言，欲殺使者。

translations.literal: The commanders Wang, Du, and the rest all did not wish the proclamation made and wanted to kill the envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders Wang, Du, and the others did not want the edict read aloud and wanted to kill the envoys.

sentences.zh: 明日，用安乃出見使者，跪揖如等夷。

translations.literal: The next day Yong'an came out to see the envoys, knelt and bowed as to equals.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Yong'an came out to meet the envoys, knelt, and bowed as though they were equals.

sentences.zh: 坐定，語世英曰：「予向隨大兵攻汴，嘗于開陽門下與侯摯議內外夾擊。

translations.literal: Once seated, he said to Shiying: "I once followed the great army in attacking Bian and at Kaiyang Gate discussed with Hou Zhi a coordinated strike from inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: Once seated, he said to Shiying: "When I followed the Mongol army against Kaifeng, I discussed with Hou Zhi a coordinated strike from inside and outside the walls at Kaiyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 此時大兵病死者眾，十七頭項皆在京城，若從吾計出軍，中興久矣。

translations.literal: At that time many of the great army died of illness; the seventeen chief commanders were all in the capital—if they had followed my plan and sent out troops, restoration would have come long ago.
translations.idiomatic: Many Mongols were dying of disease then, and all seventeen chief commanders were in the capital. If they had followed my plan and marched out, the dynasty would have been restored long ago.

sentences.zh: 朝廷乃無一人敢決者，今日悔將何及。」

translations.literal: Yet not a single man at court dared decide—what use is regret today?"
translations.idiomatic: Not a single man at court dared decide—and what good is regret now?"

sentences.zh: 言竟而起。

translations.literal: When he had finished speaking he rose.
translations.idiomatic: He finished and rose.

sentences.zh: 既而選人取朝廷賜物遍觀之，喜見顏色。

translations.literal: Before long he had men fetch the court's gifts for all to view; joy showed on his face.
translations.idiomatic: He then had the court's gifts brought out for all to see, and joy showed on his face.

sentences.zh: 複與使者私議，欲不以朝禮受之，世英等不可，即設宴拜授如儀，以主事常謹等隨使者奉表入謝。

translations.literal: He again discussed privately with the envoys, wishing not to receive the investiture by court ritual; Shiying and the others would not agree, and so a banquet was set and investiture performed according to ceremony; clerk Chang Jin and others accompanied the envoys to present a memorial of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: He discussed privately with the envoys his wish to receive the investiture without court ceremony. Shiying refused. A banquet was held and the investiture performed according to ritual. Clerk Chang Jin and others accompanied the envoys to present a memorial of thanks.

sentences.zh: 上複遺世英、天祐賜以鐵券一、虎符六、龍文衣一、玉魚帶一、弓矢二、封贈其父母妻誥命，及郡王宣、世襲宣、大信牌、玉兔鶻帶各十，聽同盟可賜者賜之。

translations.literal: The emperor again sent Shiying and Tianyou with gifts of one iron certificate, six tiger tallies, one dragon-pattern robe, one jade-fish belt, two bows and sets of arrows, patents of enfeoffment for his parents and wife, and ten each of prince announcements, hereditary announcements, great-trust plaques, and jade-hawk belts, with permission to grant these to allies as they saw fit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Shiying and Tianyou back with one iron certificate, six tiger tallies, one dragon-pattern robe, one jade-fish belt, two bows and quivers, patents for his parents and wife, and ten each of prince announcements, hereditary announcements, great-trust plaques, and jade-hawk belts, with permission to distribute them among worthy allies.

sentences.zh: 使者至邳，用安迎受如禮，始有入援意。

translations.literal: When the envoys reached Pi, Yong'an received them according to ritual and first conceived the intention of marching to the emperor's relief.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys reached Pizhou, Yong'an received them with full ceremony and first conceived the idea of marching to the emperor's relief.

sentences.zh: 及聞上將遷蔡州，乃遣人以蠟書言遷蔡有六不可，大率以謂：「歸德環城皆水，卒難攻擊，蔡無此險，一也。

translations.literal: When he heard the emperor was about to move to Caizhou he sent a man with a wax-sealed letter stating six reasons why moving to Cai was inadvisable, in general saying: "Guide is surrounded by water on all sides and is hard to assault in haste; Cai lacks this advantage—first.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard the emperor was about to move to Caizhou, he sent a wax-sealed letter listing six reasons against the move. In essence: "Guide is ringed by water on all sides and is hard to assault quickly. Caizhou lacks this advantage—that is the first reason.

sentences.zh: 歸德雖乏糧儲，而魚芡可以取足，蔡若受圍，廩食有限，二也。

translations.literal: Guide, though its grain stores are meager, can be supplied with fish and water plants; if Cai is besieged, its granary stores are limited—second.
translations.idiomatic: Guide's granaries may be low, but fish and aquatic plants can feed the city. If Caizhou is besieged, its stores are limited—that is the second reason.

sentences.zh: 大兵所以去歸德者，非畏我也，縱之出而躡其後，舍其難而就其易者攻焉，三也。

translations.literal: The reason the great army left Guide is not that they fear me; they let us out and then follow at our heels, abandoning the hard target to attack the easy one—third.
translations.idiomatic: The Mongols left Guide not because they fear us, but to let us march out and then follow at our heels, abandoning a hard target for an easy one—that is the third reason.

sentences.zh: 蔡去宋境不百里，萬一資敵兵糧，禍不可解，四也。

translations.literal: Cai is less than a hundred li from Song territory; if by any chance we supply the enemy with grain, the disaster will be irreparable—fourth.
translations.idiomatic: Caizhou is less than a hundred li from Song territory. If we supply the enemy with grain, the disaster will be irreparable—that is the fourth reason.

sentences.zh: 歸德不保，水道東行猶可以去，蔡若不守，去將安之，五也。

translations.literal: If Guide cannot be held, one can still go east by waterway; if Cai cannot be held, where will one go—fifth.
translations.idiomatic: If Guide cannot be held, escape east by water is still possible. If Caizhou falls, where will Your Majesty go—that is the fifth reason.

sentences.zh: 時方暑雨，千里泥淖，聖體豐澤，不便鞍馬，倉卒遇敵，非臣子所敢言，六也。

translations.literal: It is now the season of summer rains; for a thousand li the roads are mud; the sacred person is full-fleshed and ill-suited to horseback; to meet the enemy in haste—this is not what subjects dare speak of—sixth.
translations.idiomatic: It is the season of summer rains; the roads are mud for a thousand li; Your Majesty's person is not suited to horseback; to meet the enemy in haste—this is what no subject dares say aloud—that is the sixth reason.

sentences.zh: 雖然，陛下必欲去歸德，莫如權幸山東。

translations.literal: Nevertheless, if Your Majesty must leave Guide, it would be best to make a temporary visit to Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Nevertheless, if Your Majesty must leave Guide, it would be best to make a temporary stay in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 山東富庶甲天下，臣略有其地，東連沂、海，西接徐、邳，南扼盱、楚，北控淄、齊。

translations.literal: Shandong's wealth surpasses all under heaven; your servant holds part of its territory, joining east with Yi and Hai, west with Xu and Pi, south holding Xu and Chu, north controlling Zi and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong's wealth is unmatched under heaven. I hold part of its territory, joining in the east with Yi and Hai, in the west with Xu and Pi, in the south holding Xu and Chu, and in the north controlling Zi and Qi.

sentences.zh: 若鑾輿少停，臣仰賴威靈，河朔之地可傳檄而定。

translations.literal: If the imperial carriage pauses briefly, your servant, relying on its majesty, can bring the Hebei lands to submission by proclamation alone.
translations.idiomatic: If the imperial carriage pauses briefly, I can bring the Hebei lands to submission by proclamation alone, relying on Your Majesty's authority.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下審察。」

translations.literal: May Your Majesty consider carefully."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to consider this carefully."

sentences.zh: 上以其言示宰臣。

translations.literal: The emperor showed his words to the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showed the letter to his chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 宰臣奏用安反復，本無匡輔志，此必參議張介等議之，業已遷蔡，議遂寢。

translations.literal: The chief ministers memorialized that Yong'an was changeable and treacherous and had never had the will to aid the restoration; this must have been plotted by staff adviser Zhang Jie and others; the move to Cai had already been made, and the proposal was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers reported that Yong'an was treacherous and had never intended to aid the restoration; the letter must have been drafted by his staff adviser Zhang Jie. The court had already moved to Caizhou, and the proposal was set aside.

sentences.zh: 初，世英等過徐，王德全、劉安國說之曰：「朝廷恩命豈宜出自用安，郡王宣吾二人最當得者，乞就留之。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shiying and the others passed through Xu, Wang Dequan and Liu Anguo said to them: "How can the court's gracious appointment properly come from Yong'an? The prince announcements are what we two most deserve—please leave them with us."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Shiying passed through Xuzhou, Wang Dequan and Liu Anguo said to him: "How can the court's honors be dispensed by Yong'an? We two deserve those prince announcements most—please leave them with us."

sentences.zh: 世英乃留郡王宣、世襲宣、玉帶各二。

translations.literal: Shiying then left two each of prince announcements, hereditary announcements, and jade belts.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying left two each of prince announcements, hereditary announcements, and jade belts.

sentences.zh: 由是與用安有隙，又懼為所圖，皆不聽其節制。

translations.literal: From this he had a rift with Yong'an; fearing also that he would be plotted against, they all refused to obey his command.
translations.idiomatic: From this Yong'an bore a grudge against them. Fearing he would move against them, they all refused his orders.

sentences.zh: 十郡王者，李明德、封仙、張瑀、張友、卓翼、康琮、杜政、吳歪頭、王德全、劉安國也。

translations.literal: The ten princes of prefectures were Li Mingde, Feng Xian, Zhang Yu, Zhang You, Zhuo Yi, Kang Cong, Du Zheng, Wu Waitou, Wang Dequan, and Liu Anguo.
translations.idiomatic: The ten princes of prefectures were Li Mingde, Feng Xian, Zhang Yu, Zhang You, Zhuo Yi, Kang Cong, Du Zheng, Wu Waitou, Wang Dequan, and Liu Anguo.

sentences.zh: 用安必欲取山東，累征徐、宿兵，止以勤王為辭，二帥不應。

translations.literal: Yong'an was determined to take Shandong and repeatedly summoned troops from Xu and Su, using only the relief of the emperor as his pretext; the two commanders did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Yong'an was determined to seize Shandong and repeatedly summoned troops from Xu and Su on the pretext of marching to the emperor's relief. The two commanders refused.

sentences.zh: 用安怒，令杜政等率兵三千，以取糧為名，襲徐、宿。

translations.literal: Yong'an was enraged and ordered Du Zheng and others to lead three thousand troops, under the pretext of gathering grain, to raid Xu and Su.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Yong'an ordered Du Zheng and others to lead three thousand men against Xu and Su on the pretext of gathering grain.

sentences.zh: 既入城，德全覺之，就留杜政、封仙不遣。

translations.literal: Once they entered the city Dequan perceived it and detained Du Zheng and Feng Xian, not letting them go.
translations.idiomatic: Once they entered the city Dequan saw through the plot and detained Du Zheng and Feng Xian.

sentences.zh: 用安愈怒，謂德全、安國必有謀，乃執桃園帥吳某等八九人下獄鞫問。

translations.literal: Yong'an grew still angrier, saying Dequan and Anguo must be plotting; he seized Taoyuan commander Wu Mou and eight or nine others, threw them in prison, and interrogated them under torture.
translations.idiomatic: Yong'an grew still angrier and accused Dequan and Anguo of plotting. He seized Taoyuan commander Wu Mou and eight or nine others, threw them in prison, and tortured them for confessions.

sentences.zh: 二帥遣溫特罕張哥以杜政、封仙欲襲取徐州白用安，不聽，驅吳帥、張哥輩九人並斬之。

translations.literal: The two commanders sent Wentehan Zhang Ge to inform Yong'an that Du Zheng and Feng Xian had intended to seize Xuzhou; he would not listen and drove out Commander Wu, Zhang Ge, and the nine others and beheaded them all.
translations.idiomatic: The two commanders sent Wentehan Zhang Ge to tell Yong'an that Du Zheng and Feng Xian had intended to seize Xuzhou. He refused to listen and had Commander Wu, Zhang Ge, and all nine men driven out and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 張哥將死大呼曰：「國咬兒，汝無尺寸功，受國家大封爵，何負於汝，而從杜政等變亂，又殺無罪之人。

translations.literal: As Zhang Ge was about to die he shouted: "Guo Yao'er, you have not an inch of merit yet received great enfeoffment from the state—what wrong did we do you, that you follow Du Zheng and the rest in mutiny and also kill the innocent?
translations.idiomatic: As Zhang Ge was about to die he shouted: "Guo Yao'er! You have not an inch of merit yet received the state's highest honors. What wrong did we do you, that you follow Du Zheng in mutiny and kill innocent men?

sentences.zh: 今雖死，當與汝辨於地下矣。」

translations.literal: Though I die now, I shall argue the case with you in the underworld."
translations.idiomatic: Though I die now, I will argue this case with you in the grave."

sentences.zh: 會上遣臧國昌以密詔徵兵東方，故用安假朝命聲言入援，檄劉安國為前鋒，親率兵三千駐徐州城下招德全。

translations.literal: It happened that the emperor sent Zang Guochang with a secret edict to summon troops in the east; therefore Yong'an used the court's command as a pretext, proclaiming he was marching to the relief, ordered Liu Anguo as vanguard, and personally led three thousand troops to camp below Xuzhou's walls to summon Dequan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had sent Zang Guochang with a secret edict to summon eastern troops. Yong'an used the court's order as a pretext, proclaiming he was marching to the relief, named Liu Anguo vanguard, and personally led three thousand men to camp below Xuzhou's walls to summon Dequan.

sentences.zh: 德全終疑見圖，不出，系封仙於獄，殺之，遣杜政出城。

translations.literal: Dequan to the end suspected a plot against him and would not come out; he imprisoned Feng Xian and killed him, and sent Du Zheng out of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Dequan to the end suspected a trap and would not come out. He imprisoned Feng Xian and killed him, then sent Du Zheng out of the city.

sentences.zh: 安國既至宿州，用安複召安國還，安國不從，獨與眾僧奴赴援。

translations.literal: Anguo had already reached Suzhou; Yong'an again summoned Anguo back, but Anguo would not obey and went alone with Zhongsengnu to march to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo had reached Suzhou when Yong'an summoned him back. Anguo refused and set out with Zhongsengnu alone to march to the emperor's relief.

sentences.zh: 行及臨渙龍山寺，用安使人劫殺之，遂攻徐州，逾三月不能下，退歸漣水。

translations.literal: When they reached Longshan Temple at Linhuan, Yong'an sent men to ambush and kill them; he then attacked Xuzhou, and after more than three months could not take it and withdrew to Lianshui.
translations.idiomatic: At Longshan Temple in Linhuan, Yong'an sent men to ambush and kill them. He then besieged Xuzhou for more than three months without success and withdrew to Lianshui.

sentences.zh: 於是，因世英以用安終不赴援，乃還朝，至宿州西，遇大兵，不屈而死，事聞，贈汝州防禦使。

translations.literal: Thereupon, because Yong'an in the end did not march to the relief, Yin Shiying returned to court; west of Suzhou he encountered the great army and died without yielding; when the matter was reported he was posthumously made defender of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yong'an never marched to the relief, Yin Shiying returned to court. West of Suzhou he met Mongol troops and died rather than submit. When the report reached the capital he was posthumously made defender of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 既而用安軍食不給，乞糧于宋，宋陽許之，即改從宋衣冠，而私與朝使相親。

translations.literal: Before long Yong'an's army lacked food; he begged grain from the Song; the Song pretended to agree, and he immediately adopted Song dress, yet privately kept close ties with Jin envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yong'an's army ran out of food. He begged grain from the Song, who pretended to agree. He adopted Song dress but kept up private contact with Jin envoys.

sentences.zh: 尋益乏食，軍民多亡去，乃命蕭均以嚴刑禁亡者，血流滿道。

translations.literal: Soon food grew still scarcer; soldiers and civilians fled in great numbers; he then ordered Xiao Jun to use harsh punishments to forbid desertion, and blood flowed full in the streets.
translations.idiomatic: Food grew still scarcer and soldiers and civilians fled in droves. He ordered Xiao Jun to enforce desertion with brutal punishments until blood ran in the streets.

sentences.zh: 大元東平萬戶查剌將兵至漣水，遂降焉。

translations.literal: The Great Yuan's Dongping ten-thousand-household Chala led troops to Lianshui, and he thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The Mongol ten-thousand-household Chala of Dongping led troops to Lianshui, and Yong'an surrendered.

sentences.zh: 查剌既渡河，趨蔡州，用安以詭計還漣水，複叛歸於宋，受浙東總管、忠州團練使，隸淮閫。

translations.literal: After Chala had crossed the river and hurried toward Caizhou, Yong'an by a trick returned to Lianshui, rebelled again and returned to the Song, received the posts of Zhedong commander and Tuanlian commissioner of Zhongzhou, and was attached to the Huai circuit command.
translations.idiomatic: After Chala crossed the river and marched on Caizhou, Yong'an tricked his way back to Lianshui, defected to the Song again, and was made Zhedong commander and Tuanlian commissioner of Zhongzhou under the Huai circuit command.

sentences.zh: 甲午正月，聞大兵圍沛，用安往救之，敗走徐州。

translations.literal: In the first month of the jiawu year, hearing the great army besieged Pei, Yong'an went to its relief, was defeated, and fled to Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the jiawu year, hearing the Mongols were besieging Pei, Yong'an marched to its relief, was defeated, and fled to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 會移兵攻徐，用安投水死，求得其屍，皮刂面系馬尾，為怨家田福一軍臠食而盡。

translations.literal: It happened that troops shifted to attack Xu; Yong'an threw himself into the water and died; when his corpse was found it was flayed, the face cut, tied to a horse's tail, and devoured piece by piece by Tian Fu's army of enemies until nothing remained.
translations.idiomatic: When the army turned to attack Xuzhou, Yong'an threw himself into the water and drowned. His corpse was recovered, flayed, his face cut, tied to a horse's tail, and devoured piece by piece by Tian Fu's vengeful army until nothing remained.

sentences.zh: 用安形狀短小無須，喜與輕薄子遊，日擊鞠衢市間，顧眄自矜，無將帥大體。

translations.literal: Yong'an was short in stature and beardless; he delighted in associating with frivolous men, played cuju daily in the market streets, looked about with self-admiration, and lacked the bearing of a commander.
translations.idiomatic: Yong'an was short and beardless. He delighted in the company of frivolous men, played cuju daily in the market streets, preened with self-admiration, and lacked the bearing of a commander.

sentences.zh: 介字介甫，平州人，正大元年經義進士第一，時為用安參議。

translations.literal: Jie, style Jiefu, was a man of Pingzhou; in the first year of Zhengda he placed first in the jingyi jinshi examination and at the time served as Yong'an's staff adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jie, courtesy name Jiefu, was a native of Pingzhou. In Zhengda 1 he placed first in the jingyi civil examination and at the time served as Yong'an's staff adviser.

sentences.zh: 初，天祐等出汴，微服間行，經北軍營幕，至通許崔橋，始有義軍招撫司官府，去京師二百里矣。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Tianyou and the others left Bian they traveled in disguise by secret routes, passed through northern army camps, and reached Cuiqiao in Tongxu, where there was first a Pacification Commission office of the Righteous Army—two hundred li from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianyou and the others left Kaifeng they traveled in disguise by back roads, passed through Mongol camps, and reached Cuiqiao in Tongxu, where they found the first Pacification Commission office of the Righteous Army—two hundred li from the capital.

sentences.zh: 至陳州，防禦使粘葛奴申始立州事。

translations.literal: At Chenzhou the defender Niange Nushen had only just established prefectural administration.
translations.idiomatic: At Chenzhou defender Niange Nushen had only just established prefectural government.

sentences.zh: 留二日，至項城，縣令硃珍立縣事，有士卒千二百人。

translations.literal: They stayed two days, reached Xiangcheng, where Magistrate Zhu Zhen had established county administration and had twelve hundred soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: They stayed two days and reached Xiangcheng, where Magistrate Zhu Zhen had established county government with twelve hundred soldiers.

sentences.zh: 至泰和縣，縣令王義立縣已五月矣。

translations.literal: At Taihe County, Magistrate Wang Yi had established the county for five months already.
translations.idiomatic: At Taihe County, Magistrate Wang Yi had been administering the county for five months.

sentences.zh: 八月，至宿州，眾僧奴得報，且知朝廷授以權宿州節度使、兼元帥左都監之命，具彩輿儀衛出城五里奉迎。

translations.literal: In the eighth month they reached Suzhou; Zhongsengnu had received word and also knew the court had granted him acting Suzhou military commissioner and concurrently left commander of the supreme headquarters; he prepared a decorated carriage and guard and went five li outside the city to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month they reached Suzhou. Zhongsengnu had received word that the court had appointed him acting military commissioner of Suzhou and left commander of the supreme headquarters. He went five li outside the city with a decorated carriage and full escort to welcome them.

sentences.zh: 時東方不知朝廷音問已八月矣，官民見使者至，且拜且哭。

translations.literal: The east had been without word from the court for eight months already; officials and people, seeing the envoys arrive, bowed and wept together.
translations.idiomatic: The east had been without word from the court for eight months. Officials and commoners alike bowed and wept when the envoys arrived.

sentences.zh: 有張顯者任俠尚氣知義理，即謂天祐曰：「東方不知朝廷音問已數月，今見使者，百姓皆感動。

translations.literal: There was one Zhang Xian, chivalrous and valuing honor, who understood right principle; he immediately said to Tianyou: "The east has been without word from the court for many months; now that the envoys are seen, the common people are all deeply moved.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Zhang Xian, chivalrous and principled, said at once to Tianyou: "The east has been without word from the court for many months. Now that the envoys have come, the people are deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 若不以聖旨撫慰之，恐失東民之必。

translations.literal: If they are not comforted by an imperial edict, I fear losing the eastern people's constancy.
translations.idiomatic: If they are not comforted by an imperial edict, I fear we will lose the eastern people's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 我欲矯稱制旨宣諭，如何。」

translations.literal: I wish to falsely proclaim an imperial order and announce it—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: I wish to announce a forged imperial order—what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 天祐書生，守規矩，不敢從，但以宰相旨集州民慰撫之，州民複大哭。

translations.literal: Tianyou was a scholar, observed rules and propriety, and dared not agree; he only gathered the prefecture's people by the chief councilor's order to comfort them, and the people wept loudly again.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyou was a scholar who observed propriety and dared not agree. He only gathered the people of the prefecture under the chief councilor's order to comfort them, and they wept aloud again.

sentences.zh: 明日，往徐州。

translations.literal: The next day they went on to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they continued on to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時青，滕陽人。

translations.literal: Shi Qing was a man of Tengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Qing was a native of Tengyang.

sentences.zh: 初與叔父全俱為紅祆賊，及楊安兒、劉二祖敗，承赦來降，隸軍中。

translations.literal: At first he and his uncle Quan were both Red Scarves bandits; when Yang An'er and Liu Erzu were defeated they accepted an amnesty and surrendered, and were attached to the army.
translations.idiomatic: He and his uncle Quan had first served among the Red Scarves. When Yang An'er and Liu Erzu were defeated they accepted an amnesty, surrendered, and entered army service.

sentences.zh: 興定初，青為濟州義軍萬戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xingding, Qing was ten-thousand-household of the Jizhou Righteous Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xingding era, Qing was ten-thousand-household of the Jizhou Righteous Army.

sentences.zh: 是時，叔父全為行樞密院經歷官。

translations.literal: At that time his uncle Quan was administrative officer of the Mobile Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: At that time his uncle Quan was administrative officer of the Mobile Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 興定二年冬，全馳驛過東平，青來見，因告全將叛入宋，全秘之。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Xingding, Quan passed through Dongping by post-horse relay; Qing came to see him and told Quan he intended to defect to the Song; Quan kept it secret.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Xingding 2, Quan passed through Dongping by relay horse. Qing came to see him and confided that he planned to defect to the Song. Quan kept the secret.

sentences.zh: 頃之，青率其眾入于宋。

translations.literal: Before long Qing led his followers into the Song.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Qing led his followers over to the Song.

sentences.zh: 宋人置之淮南，屯龜山，有眾數萬。

translations.literal: The Song placed him in Huainan, encamped at Guishan, and he had a force of several tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The Song stationed him in Huainan at Guishan with a force of several tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 興定四年，泗州行元帥府紇石烈牙吾塔遣人招之，青以書來。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xingding, Sizhou acting supreme headquarters Heshenlie Yayuta sent a man to recruit him; Qing sent a letter in reply.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingding 4, Sizhou acting commander Heshenlie Yayuta sent envoys to recruit him. Qing replied by letter.

sentences.zh: 書曰：「青本滕陽良民，遭時亂離，扶老攜幼避地草莽。

translations.literal: The letter said: "Qing was originally a good citizen of Tengyang; encountering the disorders of the age, he led the old and carried the young to take refuge in the wilds.
translations.idiomatic: The letter read: "I was originally a law-abiding man of Tengyang. Caught in the chaos of the times, I led the old and carried the young into the wilderness to escape.

sentences.zh: 官吏不明此心，目以叛逆，無所逃死，竄匿淮海。

translations.literal: The officials did not understand this heart and labeled me a rebel; with nowhere to escape death I hid on the Huai-Hai coast.
translations.idiomatic: Officials did not understand my heart and called me a rebel. With nowhere to flee I hid along the Huai-Hai coast.
